hyaluronic Acid affects the in vitro chondrogenic induction effect of Synthetic PAMSPs and PDMAAm Hydrogel depending on the level.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the in vitro effects of hyaluronic acids (HAs) on the induction effect of synthetic poly-(2-acrylic-amido-2-methylopropanesulfonate) (PAMPs) and poly-(dimethylacrylamide) PDMAAm) hydrogels on the chondrogenic induction of ATDC5 mouse chondroprogenitor cells.
the mechanism of spontaneous hyaline regeneration of cartilage tissue in vivo induced by a synthetic double network (DN) hydro-gel.
the development of a novel cartilage tissue regeneration method, which will be useful in treating osteoarthritis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HA in the joint fluid is a key molecule in the induction of chondrogenic cell differentiation by the DN hydrogel in vivo, but the detailed mechanism of this induction is unclear.
the in vitro induction effect of the PAMPs and PDMAAm gel is significantly affected by HA depending on its concentration level.
the PAMPS hydrogel induces chondrogenesis in the ATDC5 cell line, which is a chondrogenic precursor cell line, and the addition of hyaluronic acids enhances the chondrogenic effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have found the mechanism of spontaneous hyaline articular cartilage regeneration induced by implantation of a PAMPS/PDAMAm DN gel, which is composed by the synergic effect of the DN gel and hyaluronic acids.
the PAMPS/DMAAm DN gel is a promising candidate for a scaffold for cartilage regeneration.
the HA molecules in the joint fluid might be involved in the in vivo regeneration phenomenon of articular cartilage induced by the PAMS/PDMAAm DN hydrogels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HA plays an essential role in the induction of chondrogenic cell differentiation by the synthetic DN gel.
the PAMPS/DMAAm DN gel can enhance the in vivo chondrogenic regeneration by the HA in the joint.
the PAMPS gels and PDMAAm gel are able to induce chondrogenesis of ATDC5 chondrogenic progenitor cells in the presence of HA, and that HA is a key factor for this process.
